Hi Elena —

Great to meet last week. As discussed, SparkHealth is a high-priority pilot for us and we want to make the evaluation -> purchase path as predictable as possible. I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) with an accelerated 3-week cadence that covers: technical eval milestones, legal & procurement gating items (MSA/DPA review path), order-form timing, and a recommended rollback/fallback if we hit any SOC2/data residency blockers.

High-level asks from SparkHealth to keep the sprint:
- Confirm target go/no-go decision date: 2026-07-01
- Procurement lead for contract review and preferred signatory
- Any mandatory procurement forms or vendor questionnaires beyond the attached security pack

On our side I’ve looped in Laura (sales ops / pricing) and Karthik (contracts orchestration). We can compress the SOW/order form signature if we get an expedited DPA review from your side or if Tom (your counsel) can sign off on the redlines quickly.

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_SparkHealth_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestone owners & timeline)

Next steps I propose:
1) Elena: confirm procurement contact + any internal blackout dates by EOD 6/11
2) Redwood (Laura/Karthik): send a short MSA + DPA redline summary by 6/12
3) Joint tech check (30m) during week of 6/14 to validate eval success criteria

If that looks good I’ll publish the MAP as the single source of truth and set recurrence for quick syncs.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: DPA redline — initial comments

Laura / Stephanie —

Reviewed the DPA redline. High-level notes:
1) Data residency clause: SparkHealth requires clarity on cross-border transfers for telemetry; propose explicit language limiting export to supported regions and requiring prior notice for transfers.
2) KMS/customer-managed key option: need a short technical appendix explaining how Redwood can support CMK or an operational equivalent.
3) Liability caps: SparkHealth legal wants a clarification on cumulative cap and carve-outs for gross negligence.

None of these are deal-killers but each will need an answer before we finalize. If Redwood can provide the KMS appendix and the updated residency language by 6/14, we can keep to your timeline.

— Tom Ellis
Partner, Harbor & West LLP
(t.ellis@lawfirm.com)
